source.title: Psychosomatics and psychopathology: looking up and down from the brain.

confidence_rationale: Canonical statement of the neurovisceral-integration / central-autonomic-network (CAN) framework: a prefrontal-driven reciprocal-inhibitory cortico-subcortical circuit actively maintains parasympathetic tone and is withdrawn (releasing sympathetic dominance) when the prefrontal cortex goes offline. Establishes that the recovery/restraint driver is an ENDOGENOUS CENTRAL system, not a stimulus or a conspecific -- the key premise for an offset-triggered, non-social, non-prediction recovery mechanism. It is a conceptual review (not a direct test of offset-triggered rebound), so confidence is moderate.
failure_signatures: When the prefrontal cortex is taken offline, parasympathetic inhibitory action is withdrawn and sympathetic dominance is released -- a REE rebound mechanism that depends on a prefrontal-analog driver would FAIL exactly when that analog is suppressed (e.g. under high load / committed states), so it cannot be assumed always-on.

Sustained low parasympathetic tone (low HRV) is framed as pathogenic -- a chronically failing recovery process is the disease signature, implying the REE analog must be able to fail (perseverative non-recovery) as a modelled failure mode, not just succeed.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A central autonomic network (CAN), overlapping prefrontal executive/affective circuitry, regulates autonomic balance via a reciprocal inhibitory cortico-subcortical circuit; prefrontal activity maintains parasympathetic (vagal) tone and restrains defensive/sympathetic circuits, and its withdrawal releases sympathetic dominance. Low HRV indexes this prefrontal-parasympathetic restraint failing.
mapping.ree_translation: The recovery/restraint driver in REE is ENDOGENOUS and CENTRAL -- it does not require an external stimulus or a conspecific. This grounds the candidate claim's trigger as internal (offset-detection on the agent's own z_harm_a derivative) and locates the eventual driver alongside REE's prefrontal-analog control (ARC-016 precision / SD-033a lateral-PFC), while the minimal V3 form needs only the offset-triggered recovery-rate boost. It cleanly separates the recovery mechanism from MECH-355 soothing (whose driver is a conspecific) and from MECH-303/304 safety (a learned predictor).
mapping.mapping_caveat: This is a conceptual/review framework, not a measurement of offset-triggered rebound; it supports the EXISTENCE and CENTRAL-ENDOGENOUS LOCATION of an active parasympathetic-recovery driver, not the specific REE update rule. The prefrontal-vagal anatomy maps only analogically onto REE's precision/PFC-analog control; the minimal V3 rebound mechanism deliberately does not instantiate the full CAN.
mapping.source_context: Review/theory in psychoneuroendocrinology spanning human and animal evidence; HRV as the index of central parasympathetic regulation.

confidence_components.notes: High-citation canonical framework review; supports the endogenous-central-driver premise but is conceptual, so I weight it as framing evidence rather than a direct test. Transfer risk moderate-high (prefrontal-vagal anatomy -> REE precision/PFC-analog is an analogy).
